result: Warm plants copies keep one build tag per copy (plants-warm-<k>); verdicts identical cold and warm on 5 files plus a left-mutant check; wall median 760 s cold -> 600 s warm (paired median -17%), warm baseline so 194 s -> 53 s when the previous run left the product crates unchanged

rulings.item: Next step toward the ~45%: the loader-side builds (ld-so, ldconfig-bin, localedef-bin) each build niji-boundary with their own feature set in target/product/ld-pie, so any product-crate change (every product mutant, and the next run's baseline after one) compiles boundary three more times (~57 s each on 12 CPUs)
rulings.recommendation: a product-build story to build them without three boundary builds, measured per mutant build; then cache libc-archive post-processing (24-48 s)

informational: A warm baseline after a run whose last plant was in a product crate still rebuilds what is built on that crate (~190 s): the cache holds that mutant's build and the restore's fresh mtime correctly invalidates it
Measurement slots shared the host (three runs at once on separate CPU sets), so single rows carry noise
